contexts.text: The Knowledges of good and truth are separated from them in the other life... lest by them they should communicate with Heaven, and by evils and falsities with Hell, and thus hang between the two; and lest also they should profane goods and truths... This is signified by, Take the talent from him... (). AC 4661. AC 7984:4. AR 676:end, Explained. AE 193:10, Explained.

The servant who received live talents = those who have admitted goods and truths from the Lord; thus who have received remains. He who received two = those who in advanced age have adjoined charity to faith. He who received one = those who have received faith alone without charity.
Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made () = one good from which are all things; for a talent = one.
Great hail as of the weight of a talent () = direful and atrocious falsities... because the talent was the greatest weight of silver and also of gold, (which) = truth and good. AE 1026.
Even if the understanding is not cultivated by the talents and pounds of erudition.
(This) is like the difference between him who traded with two talents, and him who traded with ten.
